head: pr17394-r7
report:
Overlayfs `stop` keys `ACTIVE_MOUNTS` by merged path. Check it.

I found two defects to fix before merge, both in the new `cleanupIsolation`/`ensureIsolation` locking in `packages/coding-agent/src/task/worktree.ts`. Neither is measured. This machine won't let me mount anything (`unshare -rm` fails: `write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted`) and has no macOS, so both come from reading the code paths, cited below. I wrote no probe and ran no tests.

## 1. `cleanupIsolation` moves the sandbox before unmounting it, so the ZFS backend can't find its dataset and leaks it

**Mechanism.** At diff lines 2123–2142, under the lock, `cleanupIsolation` renames `baseDir` to `${baseDir}.retiring-<generation>`. Only after that does it call `natives.isoStop(handle.backend, teardownMerged)`, with the renamed path. The doc comment assumes "a mount the backend still holds refuses the rename (`EBUSY`)". On Linux that is not what happens. `rename(2)` returns `EBUSY` only when the source or target directory is itself a mount point. `baseDir` is the parent of the mount point `m`, so the rename succeeds and the live mount moves with it. The `catch` that would keep the lock and tear down in place is never reached.

Backends that find their state by the original path then get the new path:
- **ZFS** (`crates/pi-iso/src/zfs.rs:157-183`): `stop` looks the dataset up with `dataset_for_mountpoint(merged)`, which compares against the `mountpoint` property. That property still holds the old path set by `zfs clone -o mountpoint=…`. The lookup returns `None`, so `stop` falls through to `fs::remove_dir_all` on the renamed path. That walks into the mounted clone and deletes its files, then fails `EBUSY` on the mount point. The clone dataset and its snapshot are never destroyed, and the following `fs.rm(teardownBase)` also fails on the busy mount. Every isolated task on a ZFS host leaks one clone plus one snapshot and leaves a `t<digest>.retiring-*` directory in the worktree dir.
- **overlayfs** (`overlayfs.rs:169-197`): the `ACTIVE_MOUNTS` lookup is keyed by the old absolute path, so it misses and the entry stays in memory. The code then falls back to a kernel umount, and then fusermount, at the new path. That probably still works, but the FUSE/kernel choice is no longer the recorded one.

**Trigger.** Linux host with the ZFS isolation backend (repo on a ZFS dataset mountpoint). Run any isolated one-shot task. When it finishes, `zfs list -t all` still shows the `…<SNAP_PREFIX><suffix>` clone and snapshot. The log shows `isolation backend stop failed during cleanup` / `unable to remove ZFS clone mountpoint …`, and `~/.omp/wt/` holds a `t…​.retiring-<pid>-<snowflake>` directory.

**Fix direction.** Run `isoStop(handle.backend, handle.mergedDir)` at the original path while holding the lock, then rename and remove. Alternatively, rename only after the backend reports stopped. Either way, don't rely on `EBUSY` from renaming the parent.

## 2. `ensureIsolation` takes the lock before the directory it lives in exists, so isolation fails on macOS and other non-Linux Unix

**Mechanism.** The new loop (diff 2022–2033) calls `acquireFileLock(baseDir)` first and only then `fs.mkdir(baseDir, { recursive: true })`. The lock path is `${baseDir}.lock` (`packages/utils/src/file-lock.ts:31-33`), a sibling of `baseDir` inside `getWorktreesDir()` (`~/.omp/wt` or the XDG data dir, `dirs.ts:772`). Nothing creates that directory beforehand. On Linux and Windows the native lock is an abstract socket or a named mutex, so no file is needed. On other Unix, including macOS, `crates/pi-natives/src/file_lock/unix.rs:12-19` opens the sidecar with `OpenOptions::create(true)`, which fails with `ENOENT` when the parent directory is missing.

The old code's first step was `fs.mkdir(baseDir, recursive)`, which created the worktree root. The `ENOENT` is not an `isoIsUnavailableError`, so it is rethrown and the task fails without trying another backend. Separately, on these platforms each task id also leaves a permanent `t<digest>.lock` file in the worktree dir.

**Trigger.** macOS, with `~/.omp/wt` absent (fresh install, or `OMP_WORKTREE_DIR` pointing at a directory that doesn't exist yet). Spawn any isolated task. It returns an isolation failure from `FileLock.tryAcquire` (ENOENT on `…/wt/t<digest>.lock`) instead of a workspace.

**Fix direction.** Run `fs.mkdir(path.dirname(baseDir), { recursive: true })` before `acquireFileLock(baseDir)`. `cleanupIsolation` has the same ordering but only runs once the directory exists, so it is unaffected.
